summary_responses.response: DiffTry (Differential Retries) is a lightweight, stateless mechanism that assigns class‑specific retry limits to microservice requests, allowing high‑priority transactions more attempts during overload while limiting low‑priority retries to curb retry storms. By embedding prioritization directly into the retry decision point, DiffTry avoids the need for overload sensing or inter‑service coordination and remains inactive under normal load. The authors develop an analytical model for a single overloaded service, extend it to arbitrary service networks, and prove convergence and monotonicity of success rates with retry limits. Simulations and a live Kubernetes deployment show that DiffTry reduces high‑priority rejection rates to around 15% and improves their goodput by roughly 70% under mixed‑priority traffic. Experimental results confirm that the measured rejection probabilities closely match the theoretical predictions, validating DiffTry as a practical, drop‑in service‑mesh plugin for microservice overload control.

summary_responses.response: The Office of Personnel Management is issuing a direct final rule that updates its Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) regulations to reflect statutory changes enacted in January 2021 and December 2023. The revisions broaden FMLA eligibility by counting virtually all federal civilian service—including temporary, intermittent, Postal Service, Postal Regulatory Commission, and non‑appropriated fund work—as qualifying service, and they also allow honorable active military service in the Army, Navy, Air Force, Space Force, or Marine Corps to count toward the 12‑month requirement. The rule clarifies that annual or sick leave earned under any authority outside of title 5 may be substituted for unpaid FMLA leave, while excluding Veterans Health Administration employees covered by a leave system under 38 U.S.C. 7421 from title 5 FMLA coverage. The rule will become effective on December 14, 2026, unless significant adverse comments are received by November 16, 2026, in which case OPM will withdraw the affected provisions and issue a proposed rule. Comments can be submitted via the Federal eRulemaking Portal at www.regulations.gov.
